rubrics.criterion: A user-defined handler type exposing only the documented serialized invoke capability satisfies the exported handler contract again and is accepted directly by every start path of this package that takes the contract, with no parallel private acceptance interface kept in place to route such values around it.
rubrics.rationale: This is the instance's central contract-drift fact: the pre-widening documented requirement was exactly that one capability, and the task prompt makes restoring that acceptance the acceptance boundary shared by both prompt modes.

rubrics.criterion: Every HTTP client capability surface used by the runtime API client, the extensions API client, and the CloudFormation custom-resource response sender requires only the prepared-request execution capability that its consumers actually dispatch, and no interface anywhere in production still declares the generic convenience request verbs.
rubrics.rationale: The transport widening is the second, independent manifestation of the same obligation problem named in the prompt; it lives in a different subsystem from the handler pipeline and must be resolved as part of the same cleanup.

rubrics.criterion: No production type in the request-invocation area still declares capability members whose only purpose is to satisfy a widened contract - the constant-returning content-type member and the no-op release member on the function-value adapter (or wherever the repair places the corresponding obligations) are gone, and no equivalent fabricated member has been introduced elsewhere to keep any contract satisfied.
rubrics.rationale: Fabricated obligation members are the concrete evidence named in both prompts; their removal is required for the cleanup to be real rather than a re-typing.

rubrics.criterion: Both execution modes - the provided-runtime API loop and the deprecated net/rpc function mode - are wired to consume only what they use: dispatch still flows through the shared function-value adaptation pipeline in both modes, and each mode reads the invocation state it needs (such as the invocation parent context) directly rather than through a widened contract.
rubrics.rationale: The widening threaded one wide contract through both invocation paths; a sound repair must rewire both consumers consistently, and the RPC mode historically read the configured context directly rather than through a capability accessor.

rubrics.criterion: The user-configurable base context keeps its current effect in both execution modes: every invocation context is still parented on the context configured through the public option, including in the net/rpc function mode.
rubrics.rationale: The option's effect spans both modes and is easy to lose when re-typing consumers and removing capability accessors; the prompt fixes this behavior as invariant.

rubrics.criterion: The package's test doubles no longer implement members that existed only to satisfy the widened contracts (the never-exercised capability members on the handler-wrapper double and the convenience request verbs on the response-delivery double), and no assertion is weakened or exercised behavior dropped while trimming them.
rubrics.rationale: The doubles grew those members only to keep compiling during the widening; leaving fabricated members in the tests keeps the over-wide surface looking accepted, which the prompt explicitly rules out.

rubrics.criterion: The documentation on the exported start points describes the capabilities an implementor must provide in agreement with the restored contracts, with no residual advertisement of capability members the platform does not dispatch.
rubrics.rationale: The start-point documentation was updated to advertise the widened capability list during the consolidation; stale lists recreate the confusion the cleanup is meant to remove.

rubrics.criterion: No private single-capability interface remains whose only role was accepting values that the widened exported contract would not accept directly; once the exported contract accepts those values again, any such leftover seam is removed.
rubrics.rationale: The alias interface is an injected workaround for the widening; keeping it after the repair leaves a second, contradictory answer to what implementors must provide.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not relocate response typing or post-send release onto handler-level capabilities: response content typing and resource release continue to be decided by probing the values returned by handler functions (default typing with the content-type probe, closer-based release, and pooled-buffer recycling unchanged).
rubrics.rationale: A tempting wrong fix for the unused content-type and release capabilities is to make the runtime start consuming them from handler values, which changes behavior for every existing handler and moves a responsibility the prompt identifies as belonging to the response path.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not silently narrow context semantics in either mode: the deprecated net/rpc function mode must not end up ignoring or bypassing the configured base context (for example by hardcoding an empty background context) as a side effect of re-typing its handler dependency.
rubrics.rationale: During re-typing it is easy to restore the loop's concrete wiring while leaving the RPC mode reading nothing configurable; such a partial repair keeps serialized invocations working and would look correct until deadline/context options are exercised.

rubrics.criterion: The cleanup does not remove or alter the same-named live members that the response pipeline depends on - the pooled JSON response type's content-type and release members, which serve returned responses and buffer recycling, remain in place and unaffected.
rubrics.rationale: The live same-named members sit in the same production file as the fabricated ones; a name- or shape-driven trimming of "never-called capability methods" that sweeps them up breaks response typing headers and buffer pool recycling.
